paragraphs.text: That is, with great difficulty he came to the kingdom, and with great zeal and care he went about to build your temple.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: Because the chief charge of the king was to set forth God's glory, he shows that he would take no rest, neither would he go about any worldly thing, were it never so necessary before he had executed his office.
paragraphs.label: b
paragraphs.anchor: will not come into the tabernacle

paragraphs.text: That is, the ark, which was a sign of God's presence.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: The common instinct was that the ark should remain in Ephratah, that is, in Bethlehem a plentiful place: but later we perceived that you would place it in Jerusalem, which was barren as a forest and compassed about only with hills.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: That is Jerusalem, because later his Ark would move to no other place.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: Let the effect of your grace appear both in the priests and in the people.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: As you first made promise to David, so continue it to his posterity that whatever they ask for their people, it may be granted.
paragraphs.label: g
paragraphs.anchor: servant David's sake turn not away

paragraphs.text: Because this cannot be accomplished but in Christ, it follows that the promise was spiritual.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: Meaning, for his own sake and not for the plentifulness of the place: for he promises to bless it, declaring before that it was barren.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: That is, with my protection, by which they will be safe.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: Though his force for a time seemed to be broken, yet he promises to restore it.
